findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization branch discards all table data and renders an empty table
findings.body: In `tableResultComponent`, when the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is enabled, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}` — hardcoded empty columns and empty data. The actual query results (`result.data`, `result.meta`) and the computed `fields`/`fieldAliases` are ignored entirely. Any org with this flag enabled will see permanently empty table widgets on dashboards instead of their data. This looks like WIP scaffolding that should not merge as-is; at minimum it needs to map `result.data`/`result.meta` into `TabularData` and build columns from the widget queries.

findings.title: Flex justify="right" is not a valid justify-content value
findings.body: The refactor replaced a styled div using `justify-content: right` with `<Flex justify="right">`. `right` is not a valid value for the CSS `justify-content` property in most browsers (only `flex-end`, `center`, `space-between`, etc. are universally supported), so the Delete client button will no longer be right-aligned as intended. Use `justify="flex-end"` instead.

findings.title: dcg_to_slow_conditions may be missing keys for DCGs present in dcg_to_groups
findings.body: Previously `get_condition_query_groups` computed slow conditions for `list(event_data.dcg_to_groups.keys())`, the exact set of DCGs it iterates over. The refactor hoists the computation to the caller but builds it from `list(event_data.dcg_ids)`. If `event_data.dcg_to_groups` contains a DCG id that is not in `event_data.dcg_ids` (the two are populated from different buffer data), `dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id]` in `get_condition_query_groups` (and `get_groups_to_fire`) raises KeyError, crashing delayed workflow processing. Either key the lookup off the same source the functions iterate, or use `.get(dcg.id, [])`.

findings.title: user_id recorded before feature check and may be None for org auth tokens
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ..., user_id=request.user.id)` runs before the feature-flag 404 check, so every unauthorized call to this endpoint is recorded as an assemble event, inflating the metric. Also, when the request is authenticated via an org auth token, `request.user` is anonymous and `request.user.id` is None, so the analytics rows will have null user_id; if that distinction matters, the event should be recorded after the feature check with explicit handling for token auth.
